##Load data

The data are simulated reading fluency scores of 12 studenrs.
All values are made up for practice. 

```{r}
#load tidyverse(ggplot2 is inside it)
library(tidyverse)

#read the cleaned data from the data folder(one folder up)
scores <- read_csv("../data/reading_scores_clean.csv")
```

##Histogram of pre-test scores

```{r}
#draw a histogram of pre-test scores with 10-point bins 
ggplot(scores, aes(x = pre_score)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10)
```

##Boxplot of pre-test scores by support group

```{r}
#compare pre-test scores between the two support groups
ggplot(scores, aes(x = gets_support, y = pre_score)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

##Number of students by grade
```{r}
ggplot(scores, aes(x = grade)) +
  geom_bar()
```

#compare pre-test scores between the two support groups
```{r}
ggplot(scores, aes(x = gets_support, y= pre_score))+
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Pre-test reading scores by support group",
    x = "Gets extra reading support",
    y = "Words read correctly in 1 minute"
  )
```

##Interpretation
The histogram shows that the pre-test scores are divided into two clusters, one around 20-30 and the other around 45-60, with almost no students in between. The boxplot shows that these two clusters correspond to whether studend received support: the mean pre-test score was 51.8 for the non-support group and 27.5 for the support group. Therefore, looking only at the overall mean would hide the fact that the scores are split into two groups.
